newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena CEO says convinced carrier will survive.
newsitem.headline: Sabena CEO says convinced carrier will survive.

text.p: Paul Reutlinger, chief executive officer of Belgian Sabena, said on Tuesday he was convinced the loss-making airline would not go bankrupt.

"I'm absolutely convinced that, if naturally we take the right management decisions, if we have possibilities like outflagging of our flight crews, that Sabena has a very fair chance to survive and to be successful," Reutlinger told a meeting of the European Aviation Club.
Sabena is studying plans to relocate its pilots to a foreign country to avoid having to pay heavy Belgian social security levies.
Pilots could be "flagged out" to Switzerland, which has an average income tax of 15 to 20 percent against 40 to 55 percent in Belgium.
He said that Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, held many trump cards, including the geographical location of the carrier's home base, Brussels.
"If I would not be convinced that we are going to make it, I would not have accepted the job and instead stayed skiing in the Swiss mountains," said Swissair-appointed Reutlinger.
Reutlinger said at the meeting that Swissair would not pull out of its Belgian partner.
